context: Issue triage workflow. A teammate added a step to route new issues to a component owner based on the issue body.
explanation: `${{ github.event.issue.body }}` is fully attacker-controlled and gets written straight into a shell command that appends to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Since issue bodies can contain newlines, an attacker can submit a body like `Component: x\nMALICIOUS_VAR=evil\nPATH=/tmp/evil:$PATH` — each extra line becomes its own environment variable definition for every later step in the job (this is the classic GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH injection). It's also a plain script-injection into `run:` on top of that. Fix: pass the body through `env:` and read it from a shell variable, and never derive `GITHUB_ENV`/`GITHUB_PATH` entries from unsanitized user input.
